draft.title: Norms, values and roles
card: Norm
a behaviour that a group expects of its members, such as queuing for a bus or being quiet in a library.
Value
something a group thinks is important, such as honesty, fairness or respect for elders. Values sit behind norms and help explain why a norm exists.
Role
the set of behaviours expected of a person in a position, such as student, parent or team captain. One person usually has several roles at once.
Norms and roles can differ between groups and cultures. People may follow them, bend them or break them, and a group may respond in different ways.
draft.remember: Norms are expected behaviours, values are what matters, and roles belong to positions.

a.q: A school team values fairness. Which is the best example of a norm that fits this value?
opts: Players take turns on the field, whatever their skill
Fairness is important to everyone on the team
Mia is the captain of the team
The team wants to win the grand final
a.why: A norm is an expected behaviour, and taking turns is a behaviour that shows fairness. Saying fairness is important states the value itself, not a behaviour. Being captain is a role.
a.clue: Look for something people are expected to do.

b.q: Jack is a Year 11 student and also a part-time cashier in Parramatta. He greets customers politely at work and does not use his phone on shift. What do these behaviours show?
opts: Norms linked to his role as a cashier
Values that Jack holds as an individual
A role that Jack was given at birth
Norms that apply only in a school setting
b.why: Greeting customers and avoiding his phone are expected behaviours linked to the position of cashier, so they are norms that come with that role. They could reflect values such as respect, but the behaviours themselves are norms, not values.
b.clue: The behaviours are expected because of his position at work.

a.best: Players take turns on the field, whatever their skill

b.best: Norms linked to his role as a cashier

problems.detail: The clue 'The behaviours are expected because of his position at work' practically states the answer. 'Expected' signals norms and 'position' signals role, so it points straight to 'Norms linked to his role as a cashier' without the student needing to understand the ideas.
